title: Gap Filling
subject: english_grammar
syllabus_note: Integrated board practice for the CBSE 2025-26 English Language and Literature (184) Section B Grammar: gap filling across tenses, modals, concord, determiners, reported speech, prepositions and connectors.

sections.title: Filling the gaps like a pro

blocks.title: Every gap has a clue
blocks.body:
*The Statue of Unity ____ (a) the tallest statue in ____ (b) world. It was built ____ (c) honour of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel ____ (d) stands on an island in the Narmada.*

Each blank tells you what it needs: (a) a verb that agrees with *statue* → **is**; (b) a determiner before a unique thing → **the**; (c) a preposition in a fixed phrase → **in** honour of; (d) a joining word → **and**.

Gap filling is a puzzle where the sentence always hides the clue. In this chapter you'll learn to read those clues, master prepositions and connectors, and practise with many board-style passages.

blocks.title: A love of the right word
blocks.body:
Shashi Tharoor worked for nearly 30 years at the United Nations, rising to Under-Secretary-General, and has written more than twenty books. He is famous for his rich vocabulary, but in his writing he always chooses the *right* word for the place: the exact preposition, the exact connector, the exact tense.

He received the Sahitya Akademi Award in 2019 for *An Era of Darkness*. Choosing the right word for a gap is the same skill, used every day by writers and speakers.
blocks.future: Precise word choice matters in diplomacy, law, public speaking, advertising and journalism.

blocks.question: *He was ill; ____, he went to school.* Which word fits?
blocks.explanation: The two ideas contrast (ill, yet went to school), so we need a contrast word: *however*. *therefore* shows a result; *because* gives a reason.

blocks.title: Four questions for every gap
blocks.body:
1. **What part of speech is needed?** verb, noun, determiner, preposition, connector, pronoun, adjective or adverb?
2. **If it is a verb, what form?** Check the subject (singular/plural), the time words, and the helper before it.
3. **What does the meaning need?** contrast, reason, result, condition, time?
4. **Does it fit a fixed phrase?** *in spite of, according to, look forward to, depend on, interested in*.

Read the **whole passage once** before filling anything, because the tense is set by the passage, not by one line. After filling, read the passage again: it should flow without a bump.

blocks.title: Where the clues hide
blocks.body:
| Look at… | It tells you… | Example |
|---|---|---|
| the word **before** the gap | *a/the/my* → a noun or adjective comes next; *will/can* → V1; *has/have* → V3; *is/are* → V-ing or V3 | *She has ____ (write) a poem* → **written** |
| the word **after** the gap | a noun after the gap → you may need a determiner or adjective | *____ honest man* → **an** |
| **time words** | the tense | *since 2010* → present perfect |
| the **subject** | singular or plural verb | *Each of them ____* → **has** |
| the **meaning** of the two parts | the connector | *He was ill, ____ he came* → **but / yet** |

blocks.question: Fill in the blank: The scientists ____ working on the vaccine for two years now.
blocks.explanation: Plural subject + *for two years now* → *have been*.
option_feedback: *for two years now* needs the present perfect continuous.

blocks.title: at, on, in
blocks.body:
| at | on | in |
|---|---|---|
| clock times: *at 6 o'clock, at noon, at night* | days and dates: *on Monday, on 26 January, on my birthday* | months, years, seasons, parts of the day: *in May, in 2025, in winter, in the morning* |
| exact points/places: *at the door, at the station, at school* | surfaces and lines: *on the table, on the wall, on the road* | enclosed spaces, cities, countries: *in the box, in Surat, in India* |
| festivals as a period: *at Diwali* | *on time* (punctual) | *in time* (early enough) |

blocks.title: More prepositions that board papers test
blocks.body:
- **since / for / from**: *since 2010* (point), *for ten years* (length), *from Monday to Friday* (start–end).
- **by / until (till)**: *Finish it **by** Friday* (deadline); *Wait **until** Friday* (continuing up to then).
- **between / among**: *between two*, *among many*.
- **beside / besides**: *beside* = next to; *besides* = in addition to.
- **in / into**: *in* = position; *into* = movement inside: *He jumped **into** the pool.*
- **across / through / along**: *across the road* (side to side), *through the forest* (inside), *along the river* (beside its length).
- **by / with**: *written **by** Tagore* (doer), *cut **with** a knife* (instrument).
- **Fixed phrases:** *according to, in spite of, on behalf of, in front of, instead of, in charge of, by mistake, on purpose, at present, in fact*.

blocks.question: Fill in the blank: The train will arrive ____ 5:30 p.m. ____ Sunday.
option_feedback: *in* is not used with a clock time.

blocks.question: Fill in the blank: You must submit the form ____ Monday; the office closes after that.
option_feedback: *until* means the action continues up to then; a deadline needs *by*.
*since* is used with the perfect tenses for a starting point.
*for* is used with a length of time.

blocks.title: Joining ideas
blocks.body:
| Purpose | Connectors | Example |
|---|---|---|
| addition | and, also, besides, moreover, in addition | *She sings; **moreover**, she dances.* |
| contrast | but, yet, although/though, however, whereas, despite/in spite of (+ noun/-ing) | ***Although** it rained, we played.* ***Despite** the rain, we played.* |
| reason | because, as, since, because of / due to (+ noun) | *We stayed in **because of** the rain.* |
| result | so, therefore, hence, as a result, so … that | *It was **so** hot **that** we stayed in.* |
| purpose | so that, in order to, to | *He works hard **so that** he can succeed.* |
| condition | if, unless (= if not), provided that, in case | ***Unless** you hurry, you'll miss the bus.* |
| time | when, while, before, after, until, as soon as | *Wait here **until** I come.* |

blocks.title: Traps with connectors
blocks.body:
- **although + clause; despite / in spite of + noun or -ing:** *Although it was raining…* / *Despite the rain…* / *In spite of being ill…* (✗ *Despite it was raining*; ✗ *despite of*)
- **because + clause; because of / due to + noun:** *because he was ill* / *because of his illness*
- **unless = if … not**: never add another *not*: ✗ *Unless you do not study, you will fail.* ✓ *Unless you study, you will fail.*
- **so … that / such … that:** *so* + adjective/adverb; *such (a)* + noun: *It was **so** cold **that**…* / *It was **such a** cold day **that**…*
- **Don't double conjunctions:** ✗ *Although … but*, ✗ *Because … so*.
- **however / therefore** join two sentences, usually after a semicolon or full stop, with a comma after them.

blocks.question: Fill in the blank: ____ his injury, he completed the marathon.
option_feedback: *Although* needs a clause (subject + verb), not just a noun.
The meaning is contrast, not reason.

blocks.question: Fill in the blank: You will not pass ____ you work regularly.
option_feedback: *will not pass if you work* gives the opposite meaning.
The meaning is a condition, not a reason.
The meaning is a condition, not contrast.

blocks.title: Solving a board-style passage
blocks.problem:
Fill in the blanks:

*Chandrayaan-3 (a) ____ (land) near the south pole of the moon (b) ____ 23 August 2023. India became (c) ____ first country to land there. The mission was successful (d) ____ the scientists had learnt from the earlier attempt. Since then, (e) ____ students (f) ____ (show) interest in space science.*
steps: (a) A completed event with a date → simple past: **landed**.
(e) Countable plural, a positive idea → **many** (or *a large number of*).
(f) *Since then* + plural subject → present perfect: **have shown**.
blocks.answer: landed, on, the, because, many, have shown

blocks.title: Choosing between close options
blocks.problem:
Choose the right word:

1. She was ____ (so / such) tired that she slept at once.
2. We reached the station ____ (in / on) time to buy tickets.
3. He walked ____ (along / across) the bridge to the other side.
4. ____ (Beside / Besides) English, she speaks Japanese.
steps: 2. Early enough to do something: **in** time.
3. From one side to the other: **across**.

blocks.question: Fill in the blank: It was ____ interesting book that I finished it in one night.
option_feedback: *so* goes before an adjective alone; with *a/an* + noun use *such*.

blocks.title: Gap-filling memory aids
blocks.body:
- **AT a point, ON a surface/day, IN a space/period.** "AT 5, ON Monday, IN May."
- **BY = deadline; UNTIL = keep going.**
- **Although + sentence; Despite + thing.** ("Despite is shy, it only takes a noun.")
- **Unless already has *not* inside it.**
- **SO + adjective; SUCH + a noun.**

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.body:
1. ✗ *in Monday* ✓ *on Monday*; ✗ *at 2020* ✓ *in 2020*
2. ✗ *despite of the rain* ✓ *despite the rain / in spite of the rain*
3. ✗ *Unless you don't hurry* ✓ *Unless you hurry*
4. ✗ *because of he was late* ✓ *because he was late*
5. ✗ *such hot day* ✓ *such a hot day*
6. ✗ *wait till Friday to submit* (deadline) ✓ *submit by Friday*
7. ✗ *divide among two* ✓ *divide between two*
8. ✗ *He entered into the room* ✓ *He entered the room*
9. Filling a blank without reading the next sentence, which often shows the tense.

blocks.title: Try this in class
blocks.body: Take a short news story from today's newspaper and blank out ten words: two verbs, two determiners, two prepositions, two connectors and two pronouns. Students fill them in pairs and must say which **clue** they used for each answer. Discussing the clue matters more than the answer itself.

blocks.title: Say it in your own words
blocks.body: Explain the difference between *Although it rained, we went out* and *Despite the rain, we went out*. Why can't you say *Despite it rained*?

blocks.title: Where this leads
blocks.body:
- **All grammar chapters:** gap filling tests tenses, modals, concord, determiners and reported speech together.
- **Chapter 6, Editing:** the same rules, applied to spotting errors.
- **Writing:** connectors (*however, therefore, moreover*) make letters and analytical paragraphs flow and earn marks for coherence.

blocks.title: Mastery challenge
blocks.body:
Fill in the blanks:

*Yoga (a) ____ (practise) in India for thousands of years. Today people (b) ____ over the world do it (c) ____ it keeps both body and mind healthy. (d) ____ you start early in the morning, you (e) ____ (feel) fresh all day. (f) ____ its popularity, some people still think it is only for the old.*

**Answer:** (a) **has been practised** (b) **all** (c) **because** (d) **If** (e) **will feel** (f) **Despite** / *In spite of*.

blocks.title: Chapter summary
blocks.body:
- Every gap has a clue: the word before, the word after, the subject, the time words, the meaning.
- Decide the part of speech first, then the exact form.
- *at* (point/clock), *on* (day/date/surface), *in* (month/year/space).
- *by* = deadline; *until* = up to; *since* = from a point; *for* = a length.
- *although* + clause; *despite / in spite of* + noun; *because* + clause; *because of* + noun; *unless* = if not.
- Read the whole passage before and after filling.

blocks.title: Board exam tips
blocks.body:
- Write only the missing word(s) with the blank number: *(a) has been practised*.
- If the verb is given in brackets, use that verb; don't change it for a synonym.
- Check spelling of verb forms: *occurred, began, written, lying, studied*.
- Never leave a blank empty.

blocks.back: *although* + clause (*although it rained*); *despite* + noun/-ing (*despite the rain*).

blocks.front: so or such: ___ a lovely day / ___ lovely?
